Subject: Children's ibuprofen recall: it's the syringe, not the medicine

To every parent who bought children's ibuprofen liquid from us, please read this and share it.

There is a recall on the dosing syringe packed with Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL (berry, 120 mL bottle). The medicine itself is not contaminated and not expired (expiry is 08/2027), and it is not part of the recall. The problem is the printing on the syringe in the box.

WHAT IS WRONG
The marks on the syringe are labelled at half of what they really measure. The line that says 2.5 mL actually holds 5 mL. The line that says 5 mL actually holds 10 mL. If you measured with that syringe exactly as labelled, your child got about double the dose you meant to give.

WHICH BOXES
Only lots CV6114A and CV6114B. The lot number is printed on the bottom of the box, so check that first. If your box has a different lot number, or it's a different brand, this recall is not about your box.

WHAT TO DO
1. Stop using the syringe that came in the box and throw it out.
2. If you already gave any doses with that syringe, do not give another dose until the poison centre or your doctor says it's ok.
3. If you have any doubt about how much your child got, call the Ontario Poison Centre at 1-800-268-9017, any time, day or night. They will ask about your child's weight, how much was given and when, and they will assess your child.
4. Call 911 or go to the ER right away if your child is very sleepy or hard to wake, is vomiting blood, is not peeing, or has a seizure.

I know many of you are asking in the comments whether your own child is ok. I can't answer that safely over Facebook. It depends on the child's weight, how many doses they had and their kidneys, and that is exactly what the poison centre is there to assess.

REPLACEMENT SYRINGES AND REFUNDS
Correctly marked replacement syringes are expected at the pharmacy today, Monday, before noon. They are free for anyone, no receipt needed. If you would rather return the product, you can bring it back for a full refund. We are also opening extra hours this Saturday, 10 to 4, for exchanges.

WHEN WE FOUND OUT
The manufacturer's recall notice reached us on the evening of Friday, Nov 6. On Saturday morning we took the remaining bottles off the shelf and put signs on the front door and in the kids' aisle. This product is sold off the shelf without a prescription, so for most of these sales we have no name or phone number to call. That is why I'm posting here, and why I'm asking you to pass this on to anyone you know who shops with us.

If you have questions about your box or the syringe, come in and ask for me.

Rania Haddad, Pharmacist
Cedarbrook Pharmacy

Don't use that syringe. If you already gave doses with it, hold the next dose and call the Ontario Poison Centre at 1-800-268-9017, and they will assess your child. Go to the ER or call 911 if your child is very sleepy or hard to wake, is vomiting blood, is not peeing, or has a seizure.

Full details are on the Cedarbrook Pharmacy page. Free replacement syringes are expected today before noon, no receipt needed.
